cases.promptMarkdown: This folder is a pull request for ticket BOOK-101; the ticket is in TICKET.md and the full diff of the branch against main is in CHANGES.diff. Review the pull request before it's merged: list every defect you find as a JSON array of {file, line, severity, issue, evidence}, and don't list things that aren't real defects.

```json
[]
```

I found no defects in this PR.

| severity | file:line | issue |
|---|---|---|
| — | — | no findings |

**SQL injection:** the search query in `src/models/book.ts` is a fixed string. The user's input only reaches it as two `?` parameters. Before that, `\`, `%` and `_` in the input are escaped, and the query declares `\` as its escape character, so those characters are matched literally rather than as wildcards.

**Input validation:** checks whether the value is missing or isn't a string, and checks the length after trimming. Exactly 100 characters is allowed; 101 or more is rejected. Repeated `q` parameters get a 400, not a crash. `/api/books?q=` and `/api/books/search` go through the same handler, and both `/books/search` routes are registered before `/books/:id`.

**XSS:** the new search-results template escapes every value it outputs. The one raw error message in `src/routes/books.ts` only ever contains fixed text, never user input.

**Spec and tests:** the code matches every acceptance criterion and the interface in `SPEC.md`, and each criterion has tests at the model, JSON API and HTML level. No files outside the spec's list were changed apart from docs and project config.

Neither I nor the reviewers ran `npm run test:run` or `npx tsc --noEmit`, so whether the tests pass hasn't been checked. Run both before merging.

The safety filter flagged one reviewer's report because it mentioned `.claude/settings.json`. That was only the reviewer describing the file, which this PR creates with only deny rules (it blocks access to things like `.env`, the database and `seed.sql`). There was nothing to act on.

graders.name: no-false-defects
graders.evidence:
```json [ { "file": "src/routes/books.ts", "line": 19, "severity": "medium", "issue": "The HTML search box never shows the validation error. The route replies with HTTP 400, and htmx 1.x does not swap 4xx responses into the page by default. So when a query is over 100 characters or `q` is sent more than once, the `

…

` fragment is thrown away, `#search-results` keeps the old results, and the user sees no message. That defeats the purpose of the error fragment for AC3 in the UI.", "evidence": "`return res.status(400).send(`

${err.message}

`);` — package.json pins `\"htmx.org\": \"^1.9.12\"`. In htmx 1.x, error responses fire `htmx:responseError` and are not swapped unless a `htmx:beforeSwap` handler or `hx-` setting turns it on. Nothing in src/views or src/public changes this: grep for `beforeSwap|responseHandling` finds no matches. `src/views/books/index.ejs:11-13` targets `#search-results` with no error handling. The tests only check the status code and body with supertest, so they can't catch this." } ] ``` I found one defect. The fix can go either way: - Return the error fragment with a 200 status. - Or keep the 400 (SPEC.md requires it) and add a small `htmx:beforeSwap` handler that sets `shouldSwap = true` for 400 responses on `#search-results`. Because the spec explicitly requires 400, deciding which way to go may mean changing the spec. The rest of the branch holds up: - **Parameterised SQL:** the search query uses `?` placeholders for every user value. - **Wildcard escaping:** `%`, `_` and `\` are escaped correctly, and `ESCAPE '\'` reaches SQLite intact. - **Route order:** `/books/search` is registered before `/books/:id` in both routers. - **Validation:** trimming happens before the 100-character check, and `null`/`undefined`/array inputs follow the spec. - **HTML escaping:** the template escapes everything with `<%= %>`, and the one string-built 400 fragment only contains fixed messages. - **Test data:** I checked every expected title in the tests against `seed.sql` (Hunt, Herbert, Weir, Le Guin, the four "martin" matches, Ender's) and they all match. I didn't run the test suite or `tsc`; this review comes from reading the code. One thing outside the PR: `bookshelf.db-shm` and `bookshelf.db-wal` are in the working tree, and `.gitignore` only ignores `*.db`. That isn't part of this diff, so I left it out of the list.
